a-plugin-runs-by-its-redhat-path @ manifests/filesystem_lib64.pp:1-2: baseline header states the class is an Ubuntu compatibility measure for nagios plugin invocation; baseline consumers confirm the RedHat path is invoked (files/sysmon/check_http_ssl_cert.sh calls /usr/lib64/nagios/plugins/check_http, check_package_count.sh calls .../check_file_age, sysmon_base.pp:95,104 deploy plugins there). mutates declares the apt install of monitoring-plugins-basic (the action's only change besides its dependencies); it stands in for packages_base.pp:26-27, which installs monitoring-plugins-standard on Debian (depends on -basic, which ships check_disk). The effect runs check_disk by its /usr/lib64/nagios/plugins path and expects 'DISK OK' (the plugin's result through the link, not apt's output; the pipe through cut masks check_disk's rc but the stdout match still requires an OK status). Negative on the clean node (path absent), passes after apply.

purpose covered: Purpose (RedHat plugin path /usr/lib64/nagios must reach Ubuntu's /usr/lib/nagios) matches the baseline header (lines 1-2) and code (directory + link). The checks test the declared state (directory root:root, link target exact) and the job itself: a real Ubuntu plugin invoked by its RedHat path runs and returns DISK OK. Nothing the lab can exercise is left out: the class has no parameters, no service, and is Debian-only in node_base, so no uncovered list is needed; writes into the link by sysmon_base are sysmon_base's behaviour, not this class's.
